subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Partograph, Bishop Score, Third Stage and Perineal Tears

steps.tx: The graphic labour record plotting dilation against alert and action lines is the **partograph alert line**. Crossing to the right of the alert line warns of slow progress needing referral or review. The action line, four hours later, mandates intervention decisions. The alert line starts at 4 centimetres in the classic WHO chart and advances one centimetre per hour.
steps.say: The partograph alert line warns of slow progress, with the action line four hours later.

vis.alt: Partograph with alert and action lines.
vis.caption: Partograph. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The five feature score predicting induction success by cervical favourability is the **Bishop score**. Dilatation, effacement, station, consistency and position each score to thirteen. Scores of eight or more predict vaginal delivery like spontaneous labour. Station scores as centimetres above or below the spines converted to the minus five to plus three scale.
steps.say: The Bishop score predicts induction success, with eight or more favouring vaginal delivery.

steps.tx: The third stage is managed before it can become a haemorrhage. **Active management of third stage** combines a uterotonic at the birth, controlled cord traction and assessment of tone, cutting postpartum blood loss compared with waiting for natural separation. Its components travel as a bundle in guidelines because trials tested them together. In low risk women choosing physiological care, the difference and the trade offs are discussed honestly beforehand.
steps.say: Active management of the third stage bundles a uterotonic, controlled cord traction and tone checks. It reduces postpartum blood loss.

vis.alt: Image showing active management of the third stage of labour with controlled cord traction.
vis.caption: Controlled cord traction is shown after a uterotonic at the third stage of labour. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Uterotonic, controlled cord traction and uterine massage preventing haemorrhage form **active management of third stage**. It halves postpartum haemorrhage compared with expectant care. Oxytocin ten units is its cornerstone drug. Controlled cord traction is applied only with a contraction and counter pressure guarding the uterus above the pubis.
steps.say: Active management of third stage halves postpartum haemorrhage with oxytocin.

steps.tx: A cut to enlarge the vaginal opening at crowning is an **episiotomy**. Mediolateral cuts protect the anal sphincter better than midline ones. Routine use is abandoned; restricted use for fetal distress or instruments remains. Mediolateral episiotomy angles 45 to 60 degrees from the midline at crowning to miss the sphincter.
steps.say: Episiotomy is now restricted, with mediolateral cuts protecting the sphincter better.

steps.tx: Tears are graded one to four by depth, with third and fourth degree involving sphincter and mucosa as **perineal tears** classification. Sphincter tears need theatre repair and structured follow up. Missing them causes incontinence. Third degree tears split into 3a, 3b and 3c by how much sphincter and whether the internal sphincter is torn.
steps.say: Perineal tears grade to four, with sphincter tears needing theatre repair.

steps.tx: Lengthening cord, a gush of blood and the uterus rising globular signal **placental separation**. Traction before these signs risks uterine inversion. Brandt Andrews technique guards the uterus while delivering the placenta. The uterus changing from discoid to globular and rising in the abdomen is the sign textbooks name first.
steps.say: Placental separation signals cord lengthening, a gush and a globular rising uterus.

steps.tx: Retained placenta beyond thirty minutes needs manual removal in theatre, termed **retained placenta**. Accreta is considered when no cleavage plane is found. Antibiotic cover and blood readiness accompany the procedure. Oxytocin infusion and gentle traction precede manual removal, and placenta accreta is suspected when no plane opens.
steps.say: Retained placenta beyond thirty minutes needs manual removal in theatre.

steps.tx: Cervical dilation expected at one centimetre per hour in classic teaching is now relaxed, reflecting **modern dilation expectations**. Slower progress with a well fetus and mother is observed longer. The labour care guide encodes this patience. Zhang data showed many normal women take over six hours to move from 4 to 5 centimetres.
steps.say: Modern dilation expectations observe slower progress longer with a well fetus.

steps.tx: Fetal heart, contractions, liquor and maternal vitals share the partograph because **multiparameter plotting** catches deterioration early. Meconium, moulding and urine output add context. A partograph is a communication tool as much as a record. Liquor colour is charted at every vaginal examination, and fresh meconium with an abnormal trace speeds delivery.
steps.say: Multiparameter plotting on the partograph catches deterioration and communicates it early.
